_readme: An authored 89-minute stream with THREE chapters, for §9.4's map-reduce.
Ground truth by construction, like tests/fixtures/*/manifest.json. Tests read
this file; they never hardcode. Nothing here is measured from anything -- the
chapter spans, the recurring phrase counts and the open loops are decisions,
and the code under test has to rediscover them.
MEDIA-FREE ON PURPOSE. `digest/chapters.py`'s silence input reads
`signal_series` through §6.4's speech gate and never touches audio, so this
fixture writes the arrays directly. No ffmpeg, no Ollama, no network: it runs
on a fresh clone. The speech fixture still covers §9.3 against REAL measured
audio; what it cannot have is more than one chapter, which is the whole shape
WHY BURSTS AND PAUSES RATHER THAN A FLAT LEVEL. `derived.speech_gate` is
`rms > rolling_mean + vad.margin_db`, so a constant level can never exceed its
own rolling baseline and a flat 'speech' stretch would read as silence
everywhere. Real speech alternates, the baseline settles between the two, and
the gate separates them. The levels below were chosen to satisfy the gate AS
IT SHIPS -- see tests/fixtures/transcript.py, which asserts the separation

notes: Utterance times are the START of a segment; tests/fixtures/transcript.py gives
each one a duration from its word count. They are placed well inside the
chapters and never inside a silence gap -- a segment overlapping a gap would
make the authored boundary ambiguous rather than exercising it.
Utterance spacing is DELIBERATELY irrelevant to the silence input. The signal
arrays carry the burst/pause pattern across a whole chapter and drop to the
silence level only inside the authored gaps, so the transcript samples the
conversation rather than defining it -- which is how a real transcript relates
